result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use message events for directed participant communication, signal events for broadcasts, and timer events for stated dates, durations or cycles.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant enters information or other inputs as a distinct action: Model that action as a separate activity in the appropriate sequence; do not omit it or absorb it into another activity.

When the description lays out activities in an order, or requires several activities to finish before a later stage or process end.: Connect the activities with sequence flows that preserve the stated order; when every required activity must finish before proceeding, synchronize their paths with a parallel gateway.

When the description says work proceeds until a condition is met and specifies the result of meeting it: Model the stated result explicitly on the path where the condition is satisfied, before the process ends.

When the description explicitly names multiple operations or specifies an activity’s object or recipient: Retain those stated details in the corresponding BPMN activity label so the label does not broaden or narrow the described work.
